p.src: After her quarrel with Baoyu, Lin Daiyu regretted it herself, but saw no reason why she should go and make up with him; thus she brooded day and night, feeling as though she had lost something. Zijuan guessed what was on her mind and advised her, “As for what happened the other day, miss, you really were a little too impulsive. Others may not know Baoyu’s temperament, but surely we do. It isn’t as though there hasn’t been trouble over that jade once or twice before.” Daiyu spat contemptuously. “So now you take his side and come blaming me. How was I impulsive?” Zijuan laughed. “Why did you cut off that tassel for no reason, then? If Baoyu was three parts to blame, miss, you were seven. I have always seen how good he is to you; things only turn out this way because you are so touchy and are forever finding fault with him.”

p.src: Lin Daiyu was about to reply when someone called for the gate to be opened outside the courtyard. Zijuan listened for a moment and laughed. “That is Baoyu’s voice. He must have come to apologize.” Hearing this, Lin Daiyu said, “Don’t open the gate!” “There you go again, miss,” said Zijuan. How could we leave him to be scorched beneath that blazing sun on such a hot day?” Even as she spoke, she went out to open the gate, and there stood Baoyu indeed. As she ushered him in, she laughed and said, “I thought Second Master Bao would never darken our door again, yet here you are after all.” Baoyu laughed. “You have made a great affair out of the smallest thing. Why should I stop coming when nothing is really wrong? Even if I died, my spirit would come a hundred times a day. Is my cousin much better now?” “Her bodily illness is better,” said Zijuan, “but the anger in her heart is not.” Baoyu laughed. “I know what she is angry about.” Speaking as he went in, he found Lin Daiyu weeping on the bed again.

p.src: In fact Lin Daiyu had not been crying, but when she heard Baoyu arrive, grief overcame her and tears began rolling down her cheeks. Baoyu came smiling to the bed. “Are you much better now, cousin?” he asked. Lin Daiyu merely wiped her tears and made no reply. Baoyu sat close beside her on the edge of the bed and said with a smile, “I know you aren’t angry with me. But if I stayed away and others saw it, they would think we had quarreled again. If we waited for them to come and reconcile us, wouldn’t that make us seem estranged from each other? Better settle it now: hit me or scold me, do whatever you please—only, whatever you do, don’t ignore me.” Then he called her “dear cousin” countless times. Lin Daiyu had resolved never to speak to Baoyu again; but his remark that if others learned of their quarrel they would seem estranged showed once more that they were closer to each other than to anyone else. Unable to hold out any longer, she sobbed, “You needn’t coax me. From now on, I shall no longer presume to be close to Second Master; and Second Master may regard me as gone for good.” Baoyu laughed. “Where would you go?” “I shall go home,” said Lin Daiyu. Baoyu laughed. “I’ll follow you.” “I shall die,” said Lin Daiyu. “If you die, I shall become a monk!” said Baoyu. At these words Lin Daiyu’s face instantly darkened. “Are you courting death, talking such nonsense?” she demanded. You have several sisters and cousins of your own; if they all die someday, how many bodies will you have to become a monk for each of them? Tomorrow I shall tell others what you said and let them judge it.”

p.src: Baoyu knew that he had spoken rashly, but it was too late for regret. His face immediately flushed scarlet, and he lowered his head without daring to utter a sound. Fortunately, no one else was in the room. Lin Daiyu stared fixedly at him for a long while, too angry to speak a word. Seeing Baoyu’s face turn purple as he held everything in, she gritted her teeth and jabbed him hard in the forehead with one finger. With a snort, she said through clenched teeth, “You—” But after those two words she sighed again, picked up her handkerchief, and resumed wiping her tears. Baoyu already had countless cares weighing on his heart, and now he was regretting his ill-chosen words. When Daiyu jabbed him and then found herself unable to speak, but only sighed and wept, he too was overcome and tears involuntarily rolled down his cheeks. He meant to wipe them with a handkerchief, but found that he had again forgotten to bring one, so he used his sleeve instead. Though Lin Daiyu was crying, she noticed this at once. Seeing him use his brand-new pale-lilac gauze robe to wipe his tears, she continued wiping her own as she turned, picked up a silk handkerchief lying beside her pillow, and flung it into Baoyu’s lap. Without a word, she covered her face and went on weeping. When Baoyu saw her throw him the handkerchief, he quickly caught it and wiped his tears. Moving still closer, he reached out and took one of Lin Daiyu’s hands, saying with a smile, “My heart and every organ within me are shattered, yet all you do is cry. Come, let us go together to the Old Lady.” Lin Daiyu jerked her hand away. “Who wants to be pawed and pulled about by you? You grow older every day, yet you are still so shamelessly importunate—you have no sense of propriety at all.”

p.src: Before the sentence was finished, they heard someone cry, “All made up!” Baoyu and Daiyu were caught unawares and both started. Turning around, they saw Xifeng bounding in with a laugh. “The Old Lady is over there blaming heaven and earth and insisting that I come see whether you two have made up yet. I told her there was no need to look; within three days you would make up by yourselves. But she scolded me and called me lazy. Now I have come, and sure enough, just as I said! I cannot see what there is for you two to quarrel about. Friends for three days, angry for two—you grow more childish the older you get! If you can hold hands and weep together now, why were you at each other like fighting cocks yesterday? Come along with me to the Old Lady, and set her mind at ease.” With that, she took Lin Daiyu by the hand and started away. Lin Daiyu looked back and called for her maids, but not one of them was there. “What do you need them for?” said Xifeng. “You have me to wait on you.” She spoke as she pulled Daiyu along. Baoyu followed behind them out through the garden gate. When they came before Grandmother Jia, Xifeng said with a laugh, “I told you there was no need to worry about them; they would make up by themselves. But you would not believe me, dear Ancestress, and insisted that I go reconcile them. Yet when I arrived to make peace, who would have guessed that they were together apologizing to each other? Smiling at each other and pouring out their hearts, they were like ‘a yellow hawk clutching a sparrow-hawk’s foot’—both locked fast together. What need had they of a peacemaker?” At this, the whole room burst into laughter.

p.src: Baochai was there at the time. Lin Daiyu said not a word but sat down close beside Grandmother Jia. Having nothing else to say, Baoyu smiled at Baochai. “On your elder brother’s happy day, I had to fall ill. I had no other gift to send him, and could not even go kowtow to him. Your brother does not know that I am ill and may think me lazy and merely making excuses not to go. If he should be offended tomorrow, please explain matters for me.” “You worry too much,” Baochai said with a smile. Even if you wished to go, we would not dare trouble you, much less when you are unwell. You brothers are together every day; to stand on such ceremony would only make you strangers.” Baoyu smiled again. “So long as you understand and make allowances for me, all is well.” Then he asked, “Why are you not watching the opera?” “I cannot bear the heat,” Baochai replied. “I watched two pieces, but it was stifling. I wanted to leave, but the guests had not dispersed. So I had no choice but to plead indisposition and come here.” Hearing this, Baoyu could not help feeling embarrassed, but he forced an ingratiating smile and said, “No wonder they compare you to Imperial Consort Yang. So it is because you share her sumptuous figure and dislike of heat.” At this, Baochai flew into a rage, yet could neither make a scene nor readily let the matter pass. After reflecting for a moment, her face reddened. She gave two cold laughs and said, “I may resemble Imperial Consort Yang, but unfortunately I have no fine elder or younger brother capable of playing Yang Guozhong!” While they were speaking, a young maid named Dian’er, who had lost her fan, happened to say laughingly to Baochai, “Miss Bao must have hidden mine. Dear miss, please give it back to me.” Baochai pointed at her. “Mind yourself! Have I ever played such games with you, that you should suspect me? Go ask those girls you are always grinning and joking with.” Her words sent Dian’er scurrying away. Baoyu knew that once again he had spoken rashly. Being before so many people, he felt even more embarrassed than he had just now in front of Lin Daiyu, and hurriedly turned away to make conversation with someone else.

p.src: Lin Daiyu was thoroughly delighted to hear Baoyu mock Baochai and was just about to join in and seize the chance for a jest. But when Dian’er’s search for her fan drew two sharp remarks from Baochai, Daiyu changed tack and asked with a smile, “Sister Bao, which two operas did you see?” Baochai had noticed the triumphant look on Lin Daiyu’s face and knew that Baoyu’s taunt had gratified her. Now, hearing this sudden question, she smiled and replied, “I saw the one in which Li Kui abuses Song Jiang and afterwards apologizes to him.” Baoyu laughed. “You are so well versed in past and present and know about everything. How can you not even know the name of that opera, but instead describe the whole story? It is called ‘Bearing the Rod to Plead Guilty.’” Baochai smiled. “So it is called ‘Bearing the Rod to Plead Guilty’! You two, being so learned in past and present, naturally know how to ‘bear the rod and plead guilty.’ I know nothing of what it means to ‘bear the rod and plead guilty’!” Before she had finished, Baoyu and Lin Daiyu, their consciences pricked, understood her meaning and both flushed scarlet with shame. Though Xifeng was not well versed in such allusions, one look at the three of them told her what was meant. Smiling, she asked those around her, “Who has been eating raw ginger on such a hot summer day?” Not understanding her meaning, they replied, “No one has been eating raw ginger.” Xifeng deliberately touched her cheek and exclaimed in surprise, “If no one has eaten ginger, why is it so biting hot in here?” On hearing this, Baoyu and Daiyu felt more uncomfortable still. Baochai was about to say more, but seeing Baoyu utterly mortified and his manner transformed, she felt she could not continue and merely smiled and let the matter drop. None of the others understood the exchange among the four of them, so it passed unnoticed.

p.src: Presently, after Baochai and Xifeng had left, Lin Daiyu said to Baoyu with a smile, “Now you too have had a taste of someone sharper than I am. Not everyone is as slow-witted and tongue-tied as I am, simply letting people say whatever they please.” Baoyu was already vexed and embarrassed because Baochai had taken offense; now that Lin Daiyu came to taunt him, he grew more irritated still. He wanted to retort, but fearing that Lin Daiyu would take it to heart, he had no choice but to swallow his anger and walk straight out, dispirited.

p.src: It was now the height of summer, and breakfast was already over. Masters and servants everywhere were mostly overcome by the languor brought on by the long day. Baoyu wandered about with his hands behind his back, but wherever he went, not a sound was to be heard. Leaving Grandmother Jia’s quarters, he went west through the passage hall and came to Xifeng’s courtyard. When he reached the courtyard gate, he found it ajar. He knew Xifeng’s usual rule: whenever the weather was hot, she rested for two hours at noon. As it would be awkward to go in, he passed through a side gate and made his way to Lady Wang’s main apartments. There he saw several maids, needlework in hand, nodding off to sleep. Lady Wang was asleep on a cool couch in the inner room. Jinchuan sat beside her massaging her legs, but she too was drowsily rolling her half-closed eyes.

Lady Wang was asleep on a cool couch in the inner room. Jinchuan sat beside her massaging her legs, but she too was drowsily rolling her half-closed eyes.

p.src: Baoyu stole softly up to her and plucked the pendant from her ear. Jinchuan opened her eyes and saw that it was Baoyu. “Can you really be that sleepy?” Baoyu whispered with a smile. Jinchuan pursed her lips in a smile and waved him away, then closed her eyes again. At the sight of her, Baoyu was reluctant to leave. He quietly craned his neck to make sure Lady Wang’s eyes were shut, took a fragrant Snowy Throat-Moistening Pill from the purse at his side, and slipped it into Jinchuan’s mouth. Without opening her eyes, Jinchuan simply held it in her mouth. Baoyu took her hand and whispered with a smile, “Tomorrow I’ll ask Madam to give you to me, and then we can be together.” Jinchuan made no reply. Baoyu went on, “If not, I’ll ask for you as soon as Madam wakes.” Jinchuan opened her eyes, pushed him away, and said with a laugh, “What is your hurry? ‘Though a golden hairpin falls into a well, what is yours will always be yours’—surely you understand even that saying? Instead, I’ll tell you something interesting: go to the little eastern courtyard and catch young Master Huan with Caiyun.” “Let them do whatever they please,” Baoyu laughed. “I only want to stay here with you.” Suddenly Lady Wang rolled over and sat up. She struck Jinchuan across the face and, pointing at her, cursed, “You shameless little whore! Fine young masters are all corrupted by the likes of you.” The moment Baoyu saw Lady Wang rise, he fled like a puff of smoke.

p.src: Jinchuan’s cheek burned from the blow, but she dared not utter a word. Hearing that Lady Wang was awake, all the maids hurried in at once. Lady Wang called to Yuchuan, “Fetch your mother and have her take your sister away.” At these words, Jinchuan hurriedly knelt and pleaded through her tears, “I will never do it again. Beat me, scold me, punish me however you please, Madam; if only you do not send me away, it will be the greatest mercy. I have served you for more than ten years. If I am driven out now, how can I ever face anyone again?” Lady Wang was ordinarily generous, kindly, and compassionate, and had never once struck any of her maids. But now, suddenly finding Jinchuan engaged in the sort of shameless conduct she detested above all else, she had been unable to contain her anger and had struck her once and cursed her a few times. Despite Jinchuan’s desperate pleas, Lady Wang refused to keep her. In the end she summoned Jinchuan’s mother, old Mrs. Bai, and had her take the girl away. And so Jinchuan went away, enduring shame and humiliation; no more need be said of her for now.

p.src: Now Baoyu, finding himself embarrassed when Lady Wang awoke, hurried into Prospect Garden. The blazing sun stood high in the sky, while the trees cast a dense carpet of shade. The air rang with cicadas, but all else was still, without a human voice. Just as he reached the rose trellis, he heard someone sobbing. Puzzled, Baoyu stopped and listened closely. Sure enough, someone was on the far side of the trellis. It was now the fifth month, when the roses were at their most luxuriant in leaf and bloom. Baoyu quietly peeped through a hole in the fence and saw a girl crouching beneath the flowers. With a hairpin used to fasten her hair, she was scratching at the earth while silently shedding tears. Baoyu thought, “Can this be another foolish girl, burying flowers as Pin’er does?” Then he sighed to himself, “If she really is burying flowers, she is merely Dong Shi imitating Xi Shi’s frown. Far from being original, it is positively tiresome.” Having thought this, he was about to call out to the girl, “You needn’t imitate Miss Lin.” Before the words left his lips, however, he fortunately looked again and saw that the girl was unfamiliar and not one of the household maids. She seemed instead to be one of the twelve girls trained for the opera, though he could not tell whether she played a male, female, painted-face, or comic role. Baoyu hastily stuck out his tongue and covered his mouth, thinking, “What a good thing I did not speak rashly! Both of the last two times I acted rashly, Pin’er became angry and Bao’er took offense. If I offend these girls as well, it will be more embarrassing than ever.” Even as he thought this, he was vexed that he could not tell who she was. Looking more closely, he saw that the girl’s brows were knit like spring hills and her eyes sorrowful as autumn waters. Delicate of face and slender of waist, she was graceful and willowy, with much of Lin Daiyu’s air about her. Baoyu could no longer bear to leave her and continued to stare, entranced. He now saw that although she was tracing the ground with her golden hairpin, she was not digging earth to bury flowers at all, but writing characters in the dust. Baoyu’s eyes followed every rise and fall of the hairpin, watching each horizontal stroke, vertical stroke, dot, and hook. When he counted them, there were eighteen strokes. Then, following the order in which she had made the strokes, he traced them with a finger on his own palm and tried to guess the character. When he had finished and considered it, he realized that it was the character “薔,” the first character in “rose.” Baoyu thought, “She must be composing a poem or a lyric. Perhaps the sight of these flowers has stirred some feeling in her, and a couple of lines have suddenly come to her. Carried away by inspiration and afraid she might forget them, she may be tracing them on the ground as she weighs the wording. I shall see what she writes next.” Thinking this, he continued to watch. The girl was still tracing characters there, but no matter how many she drew, each was another “薔.” He looked again: it was still the character “薔.” The girl inside had long since become lost in her obsession. As soon as she finished one, she traced another; by now she had written several thousand “薔” characters.

The blazing sun stood high in the sky, while the trees cast a dense carpet of shade. The air rang with cicadas, but all else was still, without a human voice.
Just as he reached the rose trellis, he heard someone sobbing.
Puzzled, Baoyu stopped and listened closely. Sure enough, someone was on the far side of the trellis.

p.src: The watcher outside, too, became entranced without realizing it. His eyes followed the hairpin ceaselessly as he thought, “This girl must have some terrible sorrow she cannot put into words, or she would never behave like this. If her outward state is already like this, what torment must she be suffering within? She looks so frail—how can her heart possibly endure such torment? How hateful that I cannot take some of it upon myself for you.”

p.src: In the dog days the weather was uncertain, now overcast, now clear; a single wisp of cloud could bring rain. Suddenly a cool wind swept past, and down came a pattering shower. Baoyu watched water stream from the girl’s hair, and in an instant her gauze dress was soaked. Baoyu thought, “Now it is raining. How can that delicate body of hers withstand the sudden drenching?” Unable to restrain himself, he called, “Stop writing. Look, it is pouring; you are soaked through.” The girl started at the voice. Looking up, she saw someone beyond the flowers telling her to stop writing because it was pouring. Baoyu’s features were delicate and handsome, while the luxuriant flowers and leaves hid his figure above and below, leaving only half his face exposed. The girl took him for a maid and never imagined it was Baoyu, so she smiled and said, “Thank you, sister, for warning me. But surely you have no shelter from the rain out there either?” Her words brought Baoyu to his senses. With an “Oh!” he realized that he was chilled to the bone. Looking down, he saw that he too was drenched. Crying, “This is bad!” he had no choice but to run straight back to Happy Red Court, though his thoughts still lingered on the girl, who had nowhere to shelter.

p.src: The next day was the Dragon Boat Festival, and Wenguan and the other twelve girls had been excused from their lessons and had come into the garden to amuse themselves wherever they pleased. As it happened, Baoguan, who played young male roles, and Yuguan, who played principal female roles, were joking with Xiren at Happy Red Court when the downpour detained them there. They blocked the drains so that water pooled in the courtyard, then caught and chased green-headed ducks, variegated mandarin ducks, and brightly colored pairs. After stitching their wings to keep them from flying away, they released them in the courtyard for sport and shut the gate. Xiren and the others stood laughing beneath the covered veranda.

They blocked the drains so that water pooled in the courtyard, then caught and chased green-headed ducks, variegated mandarin ducks, and brightly colored pairs. After stitching their wings to keep them from flying away, they released them in the courtyard for sport and shut the gate.
Xiren and the others stood laughing beneath the covered veranda.

p.src: Finding the gate shut, Baoyu knocked with his hand, but everyone inside was too busy laughing to hear him. He called for a long while and pounded until the gate thundered before those inside finally heard; they assumed Baoyu could not possibly be returning at this hour. Xiren laughed. “Whoever is knocking at this hour, no one is going to open the gate.” “It’s me,” said Baoyu. Sheyue said, “That sounds like Miss Bao.” “Nonsense!” said Qingwen. “What would Miss Bao be doing here now?” Xiren said, “Let me look through the crack. If it is someone we should admit, I’ll open up; if not, we can leave them to get soaked.” With that, she went along the covered veranda to the gate and peered outside, where she saw Baoyu looking like a drenched chicken. The sight made Xiren anxious and amused at once. She hurriedly opened the gate, then doubled over laughing and clapped her hands. “What were you doing, running about in such a downpour? How were we to know that you had returned, young master?”

p.src: Baoyu was seething with anger and meant to give whoever opened the gate several kicks. When it opened, he did not look to see who it was, but assumed it was one of the young maids and raised his leg, kicking her in the ribs. Xiren cried, “Ow!” Baoyu continued to curse, “You shameless wretches! I am usually so indulgent that you have grown presumptuous. You are not afraid of me in the least and now even make me the butt of your jokes!” As he spoke, he looked down and saw Xiren crying. Only then did he realize he had kicked the wrong person, and he hurriedly said with an apologetic smile, “Oh! It was you! Where did I kick you?” Xiren had never even been harshly spoken to. Now Baoyu had suddenly lost his temper and kicked her, and in front of so many people too. Shame, anger, and pain overwhelmed her, and for a moment she wished the ground would swallow her. Yet what could she do? She supposed Baoyu could not have meant to kick her, so she forced herself to bear it and said, “You didn’t hit me. Go and change your clothes.” As Baoyu entered the room and undressed, he laughed and said, “In all the years I’ve lived, today was the first time I ever struck someone in anger—and of all people, it had to be you!” Xiren changed his clothes while enduring the pain and replied with a smile, “I am the one who starts everything. Whether the matter is great or small, good or bad, naturally it ought to begin with me. But never mind your having struck me—just take care that, once your hand grows accustomed to it, you do not start striking others tomorrow.” “I didn’t do it deliberately just now,” said Baoyu. Xiren replied, “Who said you did? Opening and shutting the gate is usually the young maids’ work. They are habitually saucy and mischievous, vexing everyone until their teeth itch, yet they fear nothing. You took me for one of them, and a kick would have done them good by giving them a fright. It was I who was mischievous just now and told them not to open the gate.”

p.src: As they spoke, the rain stopped; Baoguan and Yuguan had already left. Xiren felt such distressing pain beneath her ribs that she could scarcely eat her evening meal. When she undressed to bathe that evening, she saw a bowl-sized bruise on her ribs. The sight startled even her, but she did not dare make a fuss about it. After she fell asleep, the injury hurt even in her dreams, and involuntary moans of “Ow” escaped her lips. Although Baoyu had not kicked her intentionally, the sight of Xiren’s listlessness kept him from sleeping soundly. When he suddenly heard her moan in the night, he knew that he must have kicked her hard. He got out of bed and quietly lit a lamp to examine her. Just as he reached the bed, Xiren coughed twice and spat out some phlegm. With another “Ow,” she opened her eyes; seeing Baoyu, she started and asked, “What are you doing?” Baoyu said, “You cried ‘Ow’ in your sleep. I must have kicked you badly. Let me take a look.” Xiren said, “My head is spinning, and my throat tastes both metallic and sweet. Shine the light on the floor instead.” At this, Baoyu held the lamp toward the floor and, sure enough, saw a mouthful of fresh blood there. Baoyu panicked and could only exclaim, “This is terrible!” When Xiren saw it, her heart too turned half cold with dread. To learn what came of this, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
